    Cluster cross-validation for meta-analytic data

    Source: R/rsample-splits.R
    meta_cluster_cv.Rd

    meta_cluster_cv() splits clusters (for example research groups, laboratories, countries or species) into v folds so that all effect sizes from a cluster are in the same fold. Folds are balanced by the number of effect sizes: clusters are shuffled and then assigned, largest first, to the fold that currently holds the fewest rows.

    Usage

    meta_cluster_cv(.data, cluster, v = 5, repeats = 1)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame, usually a <meta_es>.

    cluster

    <data-masking> The cluster identifier.

    v

    The number of folds. Must not exceed the number of clusters.

    repeats

    The number of times to repeat the partitioning.

    Value

    An rset tibble of class meta_cluster_cv with columns splits and id (and id2 when repeats > 1).

    Examples

    set.seed(1)
folds <- meta_cluster_cv(school_calendar, cluster = district, v = 4)
folds
#> #  4-fold cluster cross-validation
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   splits          id   
#>   <list>          <chr>
#> 1 <split [42/14]> Fold1
#> 2 <split [41/15]> Fold2
#> 3 <split [42/14]> Fold3
#> 4 <split [43/13]> Fold4
